explanation:
The debtors ledger (or accounts receivable ledger) records transactions involving customers who owe money to the business. Sales invoices are the primary source documents used to record these transactions, as they detail the goods or services sold on credit, establishing the customer's liability to pay. In contrast, supplier invoices (B) and payment vouchers (C) relate to the creditors ledger (accounts payable), while returns outward notes (D) are used to record sales returns, which reduce the balance but are secondary to the initial sales invoice.
